classification.difficultyReason: The hardest parts require translating contextual measurements into triangle sides, converting kilometres to metres before inverse tangent, or selecting sine and isolating an unknown hypotenuse; diagrams scaffold the models.

content.prompt: For all of these questions, answer to the nearest whole number.

inlines.text: A ship is 825 m from a 153 m cliff. Eric is at the top of the cliff looking down. Calculate the angle of depression.

spec.description: Cliff, ship, horizontal and vertical guides, line of sight, depression angle and two empty side-identification circles.
spec.mathematics: Horizontal distance 825 m; vertical height 153 m; theta is measured below the horizontal at the cliff top.
spec.answerVisibility: All response circles and calculation blanks are empty.

answer.worked:
The horizontal side is adjacent and the vertical side is opposite to $\theta$.
$$\begin{align*}\tan\theta&=\frac{153}{825}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{153}{825}\right)\\\theta&\approx11^{\circ}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: A flying kite is attached to the ground. Its string is 45 m long. The kite is above a point 17 m away. Calculate the angle of elevation.

spec.description: Rising kite string, horizontal ground distance, vertical guide, right angle, theta and two empty side-identification circles.
spec.mathematics: Hypotenuse 45 m; adjacent side 17 m; theta is the ground angle of elevation.
spec.answerVisibility: No supplied answer or completed side labels.

answer.worked:
The string is the hypotenuse and the ground distance is adjacent to $\theta$.
$$\begin{align*}\cos\theta&=\frac{17}{45}\\\theta&=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{17}{45}\right)\\\theta&\approx68^{\circ}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Evie is looking up at a plane that is a ground distance of 3.7 km away and is flying at a height of 800 m. Calculate the angle of elevation.

spec.description: Plane above the right ground point, rising line of sight, vertical guide, ground label, theta, two empty measurement boxes and two empty side-identification circles.
spec.mathematics: The ground box is for 3700 m and the height box is for 800 m; theta is the angle of elevation at Evie.
spec.answerVisibility: Measurement boxes and circles remain empty.

answer.worked:
Ground box: $3700\text{ m}$, adjacent. Height box: $800\text{ m}$, opposite.
$$\begin{align*}3.7\text{ km}&=3700\text{ m}\\\tan\theta&=\frac{800}{3700}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{800}{3700}\right)\\\theta&\approx12^{\circ}\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: Jill is on top of a 75 m hill. The angle of depression from the top to the base of the hill is $37^{\circ}$. Estimate the distance Jill travelled to climb the hill.

spec.description: Terrain outline with straight base-to-summit estimate x, height 75 m, horizontal guide, depression angle, right angle and two empty circles.
spec.mathematics: The straight slope is the hypotenuse; the 75 m vertical side is opposite the 37-degree depression angle.
spec.answerVisibility: Unknown x and both response circles remain uncompleted.

answer.worked:
The vertical side is opposite and the straight slope estimate is the hypotenuse.
$$\begin{align*}\sin37^{\circ}&=\frac{75}{x}\\x\sin37^{\circ}&=75\\x&=\frac{75}{\sin37^{\circ}}\\x&\approx125\text{ m}\end{align*}$$

children.label: e
children.prompt: Ted is looking up at a hot air balloon. The angle of elevation is $76^{\circ}$ and the balloon is above a point 460 m away. Calculate the altitude of the balloon.

spec.description: Balloon above the right ground point, dashed line of sight and vertical height x, ground distance 460 m, elevation angle 76 degrees, right angle and empty circles.
spec.mathematics: Adjacent side 460 m; opposite side x; elevation angle at Ted.
spec.answerVisibility: No numerical altitude or completed side labels.

answer.worked:
The altitude is opposite and the ground distance is adjacent to the angle.
$$\begin{align*}\tan76^{\circ}&=\frac{x}{460}\\x&=460\tan76^{\circ}\\x&\approx1845\text{ m}\end{align*}$$

children.label: f
children.prompt: Bec is set to walk a 165 m long tight-rope suspended between two buildings. The angle of elevation from the lower building is $23^{\circ}$. Find the distance between the two buildings.

spec.description: Two buildings on common ground, rising rope labelled 165 m, dashed horizontal separation x, elevation angle 23 degrees, right-angle marker and empty circles.
spec.mathematics: Rope is the hypotenuse; x is the horizontal separation adjacent to the 23-degree angle.
spec.answerVisibility: No completed side labels or numerical separation.

answer.worked:
The rope is the hypotenuse and the horizontal separation is adjacent to the angle.
$$\begin{align*}\cos23^{\circ}&=\frac{x}{165}\\x&=165\cos23^{\circ}\\x&\approx152\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
